t: Marx and Engels wrote it for the Communist League, which commissioned it after its Second Congress of 1847; it appeared anonymously in London in late February 1848.
It describes history through modes of production and class struggle, argues that capitalism will bring about its own destruction, and predicts a revolution leading to a classless society.
After the defeat of the 1848 revolutions it fell into obscurity, then revived from the early 1870s and spread widely after the October Revolution of 1917.
dyk: Only one page of a draft of the Manifesto has ever been located. The historian Eric Hobsbawm takes the absence of any other preliminary drafts as evidence of haste, after the Communist League sent Marx an ultimatum demanding the manuscript by 1 February 1848.
ev: Engels writes the Draft of a Communist Confession of Faith for the League of the Just, then the Principles of Communism in October
The Second Congress of the League of Communists commissions Marx and Engels to draw up a manifesto
The Manifesto is published anonymously in London by the Communist Workers' Educational Association
George Julian Harney serialises Helen Macfarlane's translation in The Red Republican, the first English publication
Marx and Engels issue a new German edition, the first to carry the shortened title The Communist Manifesto
Samuel Moore's English translation, approved by Engels, appears and becomes the standard English edition
The first Chinese printing is distributed, funded by Grigori Voitinsky and translated by Chen Wangdao
A manuscript page is added to UNESCO's Memory of the World International Register

f.made: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, commissioned by the Communist League; Engels is credited as co-author, but the final version was penned exclusively by Marx
f.form: A pamphlet in German, 23 pages in its first printing, made up of a preamble and four sections; written over a span of 6 to 7 weeks
f.where: Read in printed editions and translations in many languages; a manuscript page is held at the International Institute of Social History in Amsterdam
f.known: The opening line about a spectre haunting Europe; the claim that the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles; the closing call for workers to unite; the ten measures of its second section; the 1888 English edition translated by Samuel Moore
